newsitem.title: USA: United Dominion sets building unit sales.
newsitem.headline: United Dominion sets building unit sales.

text.p: United Dominion Industries Ltd said Tuesday it has tentative agreements to sell two of its building products units and will continue to shrink its exposure to the cyclical building and construction markets.
United Dominion said it has agreed in principle to sell two building products units in transactions expected to close during the second quarter.
Terms of the proposed divestitures were not disclosed.
It said Windsor Door, which produces residential garage doors and commercial rolling steel and sectional doors, will be acquired by investors that includes Windsor management.

United Dominion said it also will sell its 50-percent interest in CENTRIA to the partnership. Formed last year through the combination of Robertson and Smith-Steelite, CENTRIA serves commercial and industrial construction markets with metal wall, floor and roof products.
These units accounted for $151 million, or about 24 percent, of United Dominion's building products revenues last year, the company said.
"The value of focusing more fully on industrial products outweighs the benefits to be derived from continuing our building products mosaic strategy," the company said.

Chief executive William R. Holland said United Dominion will continue to evaluate its mix of businesses and will aggressively seek opportunities to acquire industrial manufacturing companies, further shrinking the company's exposure to more cyclical building and construction markets.

The company reported first-quarter net income of $11.2 million, or $0.25 a share, compared with $10.8 million, or $0.26 a share, a year earlier, noting the latest per share results were calculated on an average of 2.9 million additional shares outstanding. Sales declined slightly to $420 million from $422 million in the first quarter of 1996.
Holland said the company's latest results reflected normal seasonal factors as well as operating problems at three units.

He said United Dominion's share of CENTRIA's operating loss was $2.4 million in the quarter, while Marley Pump and Waukesha Cherry-Burrell also reported soft results, primarily due to volume and operating issues.

"We expect Marley Pump and Waukesha Cherry-Burrell to achieve improvements for the balance of the year and, with United Dominion's backlog currently nine percent higher than a year ago, we anticipate strong results in the months ahead," he said. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
